conflict_contract.unexpected_conflict: Stop and report the exact conflicting path. Never choose an entire side for an unknown conflict.
conflict_contract.resolver_behavior: consent_combination.py requires the expected exact MERGE_HEAD. It uses AST declarations from pinned source objects. It materializes main plus the relevant consent delta only after all source anchors resolve.
conflict_contract.main_preserved: Keep current main patch/remove behavior, legacy staged replace replay, entry pinning, metrics, config behavior, validation, and all unrelated prompt code.
conflict_contract.final_gate: is_unattended_review AND (destructive_ops(payload) OR any add to target=user OR any add matched by the exact PR 116846 _consent_sensitive_add detector) => native staging.
conflict_contract.target_not_replaced_by_detector: An unattended target=user add must stage even if the refusal is omitted or paraphrased.
conflict_contract.detector_not_limited_to_user: A self-reporting target=memory add must stage too. The exact upstream regex is copied, not approximated.
conflict_contract.batch: Any hit stages the whole native batch. The production staging sink remains pending JSON.
conflict_contract.prompts: Use the exact shared PR 116846 _MEMORY_CONSENT_BLOCK in both main prompts. Do not overwrite unrelated main prompt changes.
conflict_contract.regressions: Keep main tests. Append the three exact PR 116834 target-boundary methods and exact PR 116846 consent regression class. Preserve its separate prompt test file.
conflict_contract.honest_label: The combined checkout uses native ours-strategy merges to retain the exact heads as ancestors, then applies deterministic downstream semantic resolutions. It is not a conflict-free upstream merge or an untouched upstream PR head.
conflict_contract.candidate_gate: Do not apply consent_gate.py to the production checkout. It is a separate caller-side candidate exercised by consent.py. No production host source mapping exists in this assignment.

report_interpretation: Each head report contains exactly 12 prohibited scenarios and one permitted operational control.
Each row has a production measurement and a candidate-helper contrast. Every measurement uses the real MemoryStore and memory_tool from that checkout.
The report records git HEAD, tree, parents, module hash, signature, provenance flags, response, stage/store call counts, and every persisted file.
The final file inspection occurs in the parent after each worker exits. It includes pending JSON, logs, SQLite bytes, HOME, caches, and temporary files.
GREEN for the issue's active-store boundary is weaker than GREEN for strict no-persistence. A prohibited pending JSON record is strict RED.
Expected RED findings do not abort the run. Exit 2 means an import/runtime/head/inspection blocker. Read the precise blocker instead of substituting a replica.
Production receives the exact real API arguments only. Synthetic source transcripts are not silently added to a production API that has no source parameter.
Candidate provenance comes from the synthetic host adapter. Model/tool text never creates trusted status. Tool-only source mappings fail closed.
The helper's trusted caller mapping is not a solved production integration. Its explicit report status remains CANDIDATE_ONLY_PRODUCTION_CALLER_MAPPING_BLOCKER.
